question: Partly shared. Both studies identify prevalent MCI (Petersen-type criteria, dementia excluded) in Chinese hospital inpatients from clinical, questionnaire and demographic variables, using a random internal split, so the task, comparison and channel match. The doubt is the population class. P-307 samples older inpatients with chronic pain (aged >= 60, mean 71.1 years) and P-270 samples inpatients hospitalised for type 2 diabetes (aged >= 40, mean 60.2 years). Each model is built on predictors specific to its population: pain level, pain sites and pain duration in P-307; diabetic nephropathy and retinopathy in P-270. Condition 1 fails if a comorbidity-defined sampling frame counts as a population class, as 'Parkinson's patients' does in the brief's example. It holds if the population class refers to the kind of MCI behind the label, which is general Petersen-type MCI in both. P-307 itself sets its result beside a 'diabetes-based MCI prediction model' as a comparator, which supports reading the two as one question. Allowed differences: cohort, predictor set, reference instrument (MoCA < 26 against education-adjusted MMSE), architecture and sample size.

figures.P-307: XGBoost test AUC 0.925, printed 95% CI 0.863-0.995 (test n = 184). Check by Hanley-McNeil at the approximate test split of 51 MCI / 133 non-MCI (27.6% prevalence; the split is not printed): Q1 = 0.925/1.075 = 0.8605, Q2 = 2(0.925^2)/1.925 = 0.8890, SE^2 = [0.925*0.075 + 50*(0.8605-0.8556) + 132*(0.8890-0.8556)]/6783, SE = 0.026, CI [0.873, 0.977], consistent with the printed interval. Logistic regression test AUC 0.895 (0.829-0.966).
figures.P-270: Decision tree (CHAID) validation AUC 0.67, printed 95% CI 0.61-0.74 (validation n = 296: 83 cases / 213 controls). Hanley-McNeil check: Q1 = 0.5038, Q2 = 0.5376, SE = 0.037, CI [0.599, 0.742], consistent with the printed interval. Multivariate logistic regression validation AUC 0.69 (0.62-0.75). Training AUCs are 0.75 (0.71-0.78) for the tree and 0.76 (0.72-0.80) for logistic regression.

matched_figure_check: A same-model figure exists: both papers fit logistic regression. P-307's logistic regression test AUC 0.895 (0.829-0.966) against P-270's logistic regression validation AUC 0.69 (0.62-0.75): the intervals do not overlap, so the matched model does not reconcile the pair. No figure is reported on a shared predictor subset (only age and education are common), and neither paper reports a result in the other's population.
performance_validity: Exclusion does not apply. P-307's 0.925 is below 0.97 (upper CI bound 0.995) on an internal random test set of 184 patients. SMOTETomek was applied to the training set only, and the test set was left unbalanced. P-270's figures are held-out validation AUCs on 296 patients.

reason: On the figures, the pair meets conditions 2 to 6. The held-out AUCs are 0.925 (0.863-0.995) and 0.67 (0.61-0.74), and the matched logistic-regression figures are 0.895 and 0.69; both pairs of intervals exclude each other, and neither estimate is near ceiling. It is borderline only on condition 1: both studies identify Petersen-type MCI from clinical variables, but one samples chronic-pain inpatients and the other T2DM inpatients, with population-specific predictors. Whether two different comorbidity-defined populations count as one population class is a judgement the rule's example does not settle. If they do, the candidate explanations listed are not shown by either paper to be sufficient.
